findings.evidence: The pixel limit is max_chunk_bytes/6, a worst case of 4:4:4 at 16 bit. With Limits::default (8 MiB) that is 1,398,101 px, below 1920x1080 = 2,073,600. rav1d 1.1.0 obu.rs:2333-2342 returns ERANGE, which map_error (ffi.rs:72) turns into LimitExceeded av1-frame-resources. So a trusted 8-bit 4:2:0 1080p stream (3.1 MB packed) is refused at default limits.

findings.evidence: planes_match_format computes `u64::from(w) * u64::from(h) * bytes_per_sample` unchecked on a picture from an EXTERNAL (untrusted-output) decoder. width = height = u32::MAX with bit_depth 10 gives w*h = 18446744065119617025, and *2 overflows u64. That panics in dev/test inside the host, the process the route exists to protect, before DecoderFault::Protocol is returned.
findings.remediation: Use checked_mul in planes_match_format; on overflow return DecoderFault::Protocol; add a lying-decoder test

findings.evidence: VideoStreamSpec says the decoder 'should refuse pictures above' the declared size, but the route never compares picture.format width/height with VideoTrack.width/height. An external decoder's oversize picture is packed into `packed` (a second copy) before the max_chunk_bytes check at :301.
findings.remediation: Refuse pictures larger than the container-declared size (DecoderFault::Protocol) before packing

findings.evidence: Matroska PixelWidth/PixelHeight are accepted up to u32::MAX (matroska.rs:391-392). open_session (host.rs:948-950) then computes w*h + 2*cw*ch (4:2:0: 1.84e19 + 2^63), 3*w*h, and w*h*6 with unchecked u64 arithmetic. A hostile mkv (valid V_AV1 av1C, PixelWidth = PixelHeight = 0xFFFFFFFF) panics the HOST in dev/test before any worker is spawned. That defeats the isolation this lane provides. In release it wraps into wrong caps.

findings.evidence: decode_frame computes `u64::from(w) * u64::from(h) * bytes_per_sample` before reading the plane. A lying or compromised worker FRAME with width = height = u32::MAX and bit_depth 10 or 12 is only a few dozen bytes, so it passes the reply cap and then overflows. That panics the host in dev/test, contradicting the module contract 'a malformed frame never panics'.
findings.remediation: Use checked_mul (overflow -> WireError::Malformed); add a wire unit test with u32::MAX dims at bit depth 10

findings.evidence: Test fault injection ships in the product library and worker binary. The pub #[doc(hidden)] field Av1WorkerOptions.test_fault and the re-exported WorkerTestFault can make the worker hang 30 s, exit 86 on open or packet, or emit oversize or garbage frames. The worker reads them from env HSK_REEL_NATIVE_AV1_WORKER_TEST_FAULT. Risk is bounded: env_clear (host.rs:499) means only Av1WorkerOptions can set the variable.
findings.remediation: Gate WorkerTestFault, the options field and the worker env read behind a non-default `test-faults` feature

findings.evidence: Feature av1 enables hsk-studio-reel with features=[av1], so any host that enables the worker also links the in-process rav1d decoder. lib.rs:21-24 states this. That conflicts with SMB-REEL-AV1-ROUTE scope: 'enabling worker routing must not require linking the in-process decoder'. Any Trusted call in such a host then runs rav1d in-process. The lane 'next' defers this as an optional package split.
findings.remediation: Move the worker bin into its own package; host uses reel default and gets decoder id/version over HELLO

findings.evidence: reel-native re-implements motion-js's worker supervisor almost line for line. The copied pieces are Session::wait (5 ms cancel/deadline polling), terminate(patience) kill-and-reap, io_loop HELLO-then-jobs, quiet() CREATE_NO_WINDOW, discover_program (exe dir and parent), and admit_spawn sliding-window respawn. The ledger scope says 'same pattern as motion-js worker'. CX-CAP-001 allows one active owner per capability, and both copies already share the same defects (parent-dir discovery, uncancellable HELLO wait).
findings.remediation: Extract worker supervision into one owner (a shared crate or accord module); both crates consume it

findings.evidence: With no explicit program, discover_program also accepts reel-native-av1-worker[.exe] from the PARENT directory of the running executable. A writable parent directory lets another binary be launched as the decoder. HELLO checks only self-reported id and version strings.
findings.remediation: Search only the executable directory, or require an explicit program path outside tests

findings.evidence: spawn waits for HELLO with recv_timeout(spawn_timeout = 10 s default) and does not poll the cancel token. A cancel during a slow worker start is honoured only after the handshake or the timeout.
findings.remediation: Wait for HELLO in WAIT_SLICE steps that check cancel (as Session::wait does)

verified_fixes: Quiet spawn: CREATE_NO_WINDOW 0x08000000 via CommandExt::creation_flags (host.rs:66-68, 394-398), env_clear, stderr null, piped stdin and stdout (:494-503).

Deadline and cancel kill: exchange waits in 5 ms slices against min(batch_deadline, segment_wall) and the cancel token (:316-332, 626-646). Timeout and cancel call terminate(ZERO): kill, then wait to reap (:336-348).

Crash to typed fault: end of stream maps to DecoderCrashed{exit_code} after up to 500 ms patience to read the real exit code (:601-606). The worker panic hook exits 70 (worker.rs:214). The fault maps to ReelError::DecoderFault{Crashed,Deadline,Protocol} (host.rs:201-215).

No orphan processes: every Child is owned by a Session whose Drop kills and reaps it (:351-355). Permit counts live processes until reaped (:292-298). The worker exits when its stdin closes, even mid-decode, through a reader thread (worker.rs:216-233). The hostile test asserts alive == 1 after 7 crashes.

Bounded IPC: frame length is checked against the cap before allocation (wire.rs:68-87). Requests are capped at 32 MiB; reply cap = declared-dimension cap + 512; at most 64 FRAMEs per batch (host.rs:650); sync_channel(1) backpressure (:507). Every FRAME plane length must equal the declared format (wire.rs:512-519). Error text crosses as an index into a fixed static table (wire.rs:33-54).

Bounded respawn: max_spawns per spawn_window with a sliding log (host.rs:466-481), and the max_workers permit is checked before spawn (:483-488). Job Object / RSS cap is disclosed NOT_PROVEN in DESCRIPTOR.

Tests are substantive: worker output is bit-exact with the libdav1d oracle and with reel in-process receipts; 6 recorded aborting mutations end as decoder_crashed with the host alive; deadline, cancel, oversize, garbage and respawn bound are each checked against counters. round-features.toml declares reel-native=[[av1]], so they run in the round.

findings.evidence: Budget(Stack) and Budget(Memory) are still chosen by user-writable message text. `throw new RangeError('Maximum call stack size exceeded')` gives kind 3 + FLAG_STACK_OVERFLOW = Budget(Stack); `throw new InternalError('out of memory')` gives Budget(Memory). R3 explicitly listed 'forged RangeError -> Budget'. quickjs_contract.rs:338-357 tests only 'x'/'boom' messages.

Deadline and cancel kill: wall = remaining + kill_grace on the real monotonic clock (:473); Session::wait polls cancel and deadline every 5 ms (:166-184); exchange terminates and reaps on every failure (:408-452). Worker-side watchdog exit(3) at deadline + 2 s (:596-599) bounds a worker whose host is gone.

findings.evidence: Streams with refused filters (DCT, JPX, CCITT, JBIG2, Crypt), indirect filters or a decode_error are only scanned raw and listed in streams_not_decodable. Yet is_proven() is region_cleared && hits.is_empty() and never checks proof.fully_decoded(). A removed string held in such a stream, for example a corrupt FlateDecode XMP, makes is_proven() true. This contradicts the module claim 'the proof never claims more than it scanned' (:11) and the DESCRIPTOR 'is_proven' wording. pdf_delivery.rs asserts is_proven without fully_decoded.
findings.remediation: Require proof.fully_decoded() in is_proven (or a typed NotProven state); add an undecodable-stream test

findings.evidence: residual_in_region re-runs the same redact_region selector on the saved bytes, so a selector miss repeats and is not detected. One example: bbox() drops NaN from a CTM product overflow via f64::min/max, so touches() is false and the text counts as outside the region. The payload proof cannot catch a missed instance either: an unremoved Tj in the region is never a needle, and a kept Tj match is classed as a collision, not a leak.
findings.remediation: Treat non-finite glyph boxes as unredacted marks; add an independent residual check (e.g. text extraction per region)

findings.evidence: The raw scan(output, vars) runs before the per-object loop with no cancel check. find() is a naive windows().position per variant, so with up to 64 MiB output and 2 variants per removed string it costs O(bytes x variants) and cannot be cancelled until it finishes.
findings.remediation: Check cancel inside scan per variant/chunk, or use a multi-pattern matcher (Aho-Corasick) with cancel polling

findings.evidence: The module doc still says LZW is a typed UnsupportedFilter refusal, but LZWDecode is implemented (:87-94) and listed in DESCRIPTOR. ascii85 also accepts a final partial group whose value exceeds u32 and silently truncates it (`v as u32`, :361-363); full groups are refused (:341-343).
findings.remediation: Fix the filters.rs header; refuse an overflowing final ASCII85 group as Malformed

verified_fixes: No prior verdict. Reader bounds re-read: depth-limited object parser (syntax.rs:194-196). as_f64/as_int accept only finite values (syntax.rs:72,79). The endstream recovery scan has its own scan_budget (reader.rs:57-60, 104-113).

Filters are bounded. Flate uses decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit(cap). LZW uses fixed 4096-entry tables, kwkwk only when code == next < 4096, and an output cap checked before resize (filters.rs:192-291). Predictor rows*row_bytes is checked against the cap before allocation (:143-149). ASCIIHex, ASCII85 and RunLength check the cap per step. A per-operation decoded budget (max_decoded_total) is enforced (:104-107).
redact_and_save restores doc.objects on any error (sanitized_save.rs:342-397). The proof re-opens the OUTPUT bytes, and the short-needle exclusion is reported (short_needles), not hidden.

findings.evidence: css_references matches only the literal bytes `url(` and never decodes CSS escapes. Two bypasses follow. (1) `u\72l(https://evil.example/a.png)`, an escaped url( token that CSS engines honour, is not collected at all. (2) `url(ht\74p://evil.example/a.png)` is collected, but classify() maps `\` to `/`, so the first delimiter precedes the colon. The reference is treated as relative and handed to the AssetPort instead of being typed Denied(ExternalScheme). A CSS engine decodes both to http://evil.example. That breaks the module contract 'External ... URLs are typed Denied without the port being consulted'.
findings.remediation: Decode CSS escapes (ident and url) before matching and classifying; add escaped-scheme and escaped-url( tests

findings.evidence: URL_ATTRIBUTES omits <base href>, which re-targets every relative reference: with `<base href="https://evil/">` a relative img that the port Granted is fetched externally. It also omits svg <image href|xlink:href>, <iframe srcdoc> (inline HTML), <frame src>, form/button/input formaction and background attributes. None of them is listed in DESCRIPTOR not_scanned (only srcset, image-set(), meta refresh), so the report under-states its scope.
findings.remediation: Collect <base href> (deny or mark all relative refs unresolved), add the missing URL attributes, list the rest in not_scanned

findings.evidence: Relative references reach AssetPort::resolve verbatim, with no normalisation or typed refusal of `..` traversal or percent-encoded separators (%2e%2e%2f). Each embedder's port must implement that itself, so a naive port mapping references to project paths can escape the project root.
findings.remediation: Normalise relative refs and refuse ones escaping the document root as Denied(NotGranted) before the port

verified_fixes: No prior verdict. Classification re-read: leading/trailing C0 and space trimmed, tab/CR/LF removed and the rest lower-cased before scheme detection, so `java\nscript:` and `JAVASCRIPT:` are denied. file:, protocol-relative and drive-letter (`c:`) references are denied; control characters are refused before the port. Attribute values are entity-decoded first (`javascript:`).
The crate does no I/O: no fetch, file or network calls in src (DESCRIPTOR never list). Asset collection is bounded by max_nodes with cancel every 1024 nodes (assets.rs:153-169).
Parser panics are invariant expects only (dom.rs:292,297,322-323,556,602: root stays on the stack, elements have names). descendants uses an explicit stack.

findings.evidence: job_admit stores tickets as (jobs, bytes) with no owner, and tickets are sequential (next_ticket += 1). JobRelease removes any ticket for any actor with no principal, account or grant check. One actor can release another actor's admitted job and free its slots and bytes, defeating the job_capacity/job_byte_budget accounting. job_admit also performs no grant check.
findings.remediation: Bind tickets to account+principal+resource at admit; refuse release by another owner; add a cross-actor release test

findings.evidence: The module contract says decoding 'refuses everything the encoder cannot produce' (canonical field order, no whitespace). decode() only refuses a non-'{' first byte and trailing whitespace. serde_json still accepts interior whitespace, any field order and \u escapes in strings, none of which the encoder emits. wire_strictness_and_descriptor (tests :444-520) tests only leading and trailing bytes.
findings.remediation: Re-encode the decoded value and require byte equality with the input (refuse non-canonical), or correct the contract text

findings.evidence: The lease fence refuses only lease_epoch < current.epoch and then stores the client-supplied epoch. Nothing issues or verifies leases, so any granted editor can commit with lease_epoch = u64::MAX and permanently fence every other writer to StaleEpoch.
findings.remediation: Accept only the host-issued current epoch (==), or issue epochs from a host lease call and verify them

verified_fixes: No prior verdict. Commit order re-read (host.rs:310-411): grant and token rechecked on every commit, replays included. Idempotency is bound to account+principal+resource+binding, and a conflict discloses nothing. Then epoch fence, expected-revision compare, successor == expected+1, receipt cap, and an atomic state+receipt+idempotency write under one lock.

Adapter (adapter.rs:41-80, 243-310): replies must echo the correlation id. No, undecodable or mismatched reply maps to denied grant, refused job, or commit Unknown (never Rejected). Rejected('wire_invalid') only when nothing was sent.

Wire: deny_unknown_fields on every struct, version read first and alone, hex lowercase only and size-checked before decode, and encoder validates first. The 12 distinct codes are asserted by mutation tests.

findings.evidence: `verify PACKAGE` with no --expect-revision and no --expect-name/--expect-visible gives revision_ok = true via is_none_or and an empty checks list, so all = true and the verdict is 'pass' with exit 0. Any package that opens 'verifies' while checking nothing. The manual marks every expectation optional, and agents read this verdict as proof.
findings.remediation: Refuse verify with zero expectations (usage exit 2), or report verdict 'nothing_checked' that is not pass

findings.evidence: --save takes any path, including the input PACKAGE itself or a path outside the working tree, and the session save_to writes it after edits. The CLI has no guard against overwriting the source package or writing outside an allowed root. Agents drive this CLI headlessly.
findings.remediation: Refuse --save equal to the input path unless --overwrite is given; document the allowed output roots

verified_fixes: No prior verdict. Selection is explicit: nothing is selected by default, and unknown or duplicate providers are refused before any step. References default to Unresolved; trust_all is an explicit flag recorded in every report (harness.rs:39-49, 165; finish :651-664).

The CLI is a pure function (args in, exit code and stdout out). The example is a thin forwarder with no process spawn, window or network. Exit codes are 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 usage. Edits stop at the first refused operation before any save (cli.rs:214-236).
Expectation checks compare live session values, and a missing layer is ok=false (harness.rs:637-647). finish() is ok only when every operation succeeded.
